{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"470f60d80e0873dd0a8e4c94bfbdd2aba9c1ca226e0dec59fcac65bfa057db4b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:132","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Sharing the road with bicyclists, motorcycles, trucks and slow-moving vehicles, plus the last light rail cautions for children","heading":"C — The final light rail cautions, sharing the road with bicyclists and the bicycle rules, motorcycle visibility, lane filtering and passing, the truck No-Zone and stopping distance, and farm machinery and slow-moving vehicles","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — The final light rail cautions, sharing the road with bicyclists and the bicycle rules, motorcycle visibility, lane filtering and passing, the truck No-Zone and stopping distance, and farm machinery and slow-moving vehicles
Knowledge domain: the closing light rail cautions for children, how drivers must pass and watch for bicyclists and what rules bicyclists follow, why motorcycles are hard to judge and when lane filtering is legal, how to stay safe around large trucks, and how to handle farm machinery and vehicles marked as slow-moving.

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: FXP0049
Children should not fly kites or model airplanes near the overhead power lines used by light rail [FXP0049] [A01].
Source: [FXP0049 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Skateboarding, rollerblading and bike riding on light rail tracks or station platforms is unsafe and not permitted. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists must follow the same traffic laws as drivers, and they get the right-of-way in the same situations that drivers do. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists are often hard to see, so drivers must watch for them along the road and use extra caution. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
When passing a bicyclist who is going the same direction, a driver must leave a safe distance of at least 3 feet. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A01
Honking at a bicyclist while you pass is unsafe because the sound may startle the rider and cause a crash. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A01
At night, dim your headlights as a courtesy to bicyclists. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A01
Be ready for a bicyclist to swerve, because a rider may legally move left to turn left, avoid a hazard, pass a pedestrian or vehicle, or when the lane is too narrow to share safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists must ride in the same direction as traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A01
A bicycle may not carry more people than it was designed to carry. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists may not ride more than two abreast. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists should ride as close to the right side of the road as is practicable. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists should use proper hand signals. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A01
Riding a bicycle under the influence of drugs or alcohol is illegal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A01
A bicycle ridden at night needs a white headlamp that can be seen from 500 feet and a rear reflector. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A01
A flashing red light on the back of a bicycle can make the rider easier for drivers to see. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A01
In a crash, a motorcyclist is more likely to be injured than the driver of a car. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A01
Most crashes between cars and motorcycles happen when a car turns in front of a motorcycle, usually because the driver did not see it or misjudged its distance and speed [A01] [A02].
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle's small size can make it hard to spot and can make it look farther away and slower than it really is. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle's single headlight or taillight gives you fewer clues for judging its distance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A02
Motorcyclists are less stable in rain and wind. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A02
Lane filtering is when a motorcyclist safely passes a vehicle that is stopped in the same lane and direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F23 | anchor: A02
Lane filtering is allowed only on a street with at least 2 adjacent lanes going the same direction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F24 | anchor: A02
Lane filtering is allowed only where the posted speed limit is no higher than 45 miles per hour. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F25 | anchor: A02
While lane filtering, the motorcycle may not go faster than 15 miles per hour. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F26 | anchor: A02
Intersections carry a high risk of car and motorcycle collisions, usually because a driver turns into the motorcycle's path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F27 | anchor: A02
Do not assume what a rider intends, since a rider may move to one side to avoid a hazard or to be seen, not only to get ready to turn. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F28 | anchor: A02
Motorcyclists may shift within their lane to avoid oil, potholes or debris, so a motorcycle may come into your lane unexpectedly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F29 | anchor: A02
Motorcycle turn signals do not cancel themselves, so be certain of the rider's plan before you pull into the motorcycle's path. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F30 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle is entitled to the full width of a lane, so never squeeze into the same lane as a motorcycle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F31 | anchor: A02
After passing a motorcycle, cutting back into your lane too early can push the rider to swerve into other traffic or off the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F32 | anchor: A02
Large trucks matter to the Arizona economy because they carry products people depend on. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-F33 | anchor: A03
Never cut in front of a truck, because a truck needs twice as long to stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F34 | anchor: A03
If you cut in front of a truck and then brake hard, you cut the truck's available stopping distance in half. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F35 | anchor: A03
Large trucks and buses have big blind spots, called the No-Zone, at the front and along the back sides, so do not linger there. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F36 | anchor: A03
Follow a truck at a safe distance, since a truck is almost as wide as some lanes and following too closely leaves you no time to react. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F37 | anchor: A03
Trucks make wide right turns and may leave an open space on their right just before turning, so never pass a truck on the right if it might turn right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F38 | anchor: A03
If you break down, pull as far off the highway as you can, because a parked car hit on the shoulder suffers more severe damage. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F39 | anchor: A03
A truck can weigh as much as 25 cars, so a truck striking a car parked on the shoulder could be tragic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F40 | anchor: A03
Behind farm machinery and other slow-moving vehicles, keep a safe following distance that gives you a good field of vision. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F41 | anchor: A03
Farm machinery normally moves at 25 mph or slower, can occupy more than one lane and may lack signals. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F42 | anchor: A03
To make a wide turn, a farm machinery operator may pull to the left first and then turn to the right. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F43 | anchor: A03
A vehicle showing the slow-moving vehicle symbol on its back cannot go faster than 25 mph, so the symbol is your signal to slow down. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-F44 | anchor: A03
A slow-moving vehicle has a legal right to be on the road, so do not grow impatient when you are behind one. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

Misconceptions: a bicyclist moving left is not necessarily breaking the law, since riders may move left for several legal reasons; a motorcycle that looks far away and slow may be closer and faster than it seems; a motorcycle's blinking signal does not prove the rider is turning; a farm vehicle pulling left may actually be about to turn right; lane filtering is for motorcyclists only and only under its three conditions.
Mnemonics: Bikes get a three-foot cushion; trucks need double the stopping room; motorcycles filter only slowly, on slow multi-lane streets.
Glossary: lane filtering means a motorcycle passing stopped vehicles in its own lane under strict limits; No-Zone means the large blind spots around trucks and buses; slow-moving vehicle symbol means the rear emblem marking a vehicle that cannot exceed a low top speed; practicable means as far as conditions safely allow.
Dynamic facts: the lane filtering conditions, the bicycle passing distance and the bicycle equipment rules are statutory and can be amended.
